Existing live-owned completed-resolution CLOSED/REQUEUED receipts and their outage-only retry guards remain unchanged. The accepted binding attempt_id is real and remains nonnull even when ledger dispatch attempt_id is absent. A read-entry proves possible provider entry only: it may precede a crash before the call or a real read whose decision was lost. Receipt, terminal history/ledger and all required summaries share the actual winning caller physical transaction. Deferred guards on each current/future leaf independently verify that transaction's actual terminal row version, exact locator/binding/attempt and complete declared-ID classification. Savepoint/subtransaction row-version behavior must be proven or prohibited; transaction labels or self-invoked proxy annotations are not proof. External caller rollback and injected receipt/audit failures roll back every write. All actual immediate-cancel, generic-close, pending-reaper and kill-switch terminal entrypoints must participate; admitted/running reconciliation settles authentic linked facts under its real terminal state matrix, never this pre-send unlinked shape. Request-only cancel, applied=0, stale or losing transitions append zero rows. Append-only UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE guards cover receipt parents and leaves, with no DEFAULT partition, aligned bounded existing 12-month Q3 retention, bootstrap/pruner coverage, stable cross-month deduplication and owner-row→owner-advisory→event lock order. No self-FK may prevent approved expiry; a same-transaction row version is not permanent identity. For these two unlinked replay cases outcome, release_id, release_seq, vault_version, admission_id, source_reference_id, coordinate_step_id and coordinate_ordinal are all NULL; the real accepted binding attempt_id is nonnull. The original three-variant null-release_seq rule remains and also applies to variant (4). Validate bounded unique disjoint no-read/possible-read ID sets against exactly the remaining authenticated accepted declarations, after excluding authentic existing decisions and summaries; no caller-chosen omission or invented ID is allowed. Durable entry is only possible-read evidence; the receipt/SQL does not measure a physical provider read. Without universal write-before-value-read enforcement, fresh-view classification or authenticated terminal/no-send proof, completeness remains unmet: emit no guessed negative. Known actual releases keep all scoped links/outcomes/version/sequence checks and honest linked settlement, including immutable early USED. A late loser cannot append its transient resolution facts after another terminal owner won. Existing GUIDED declaration absence checks continue to exclude any prior consumption/decision/summary across retained fences for that exact reference. A prior same-reference USED summary excludes a new unreached claim, but must not mask a later authentic consumed admission: settle that later admission under its existing actual linked or consumed-no-decision owner/admission/coordinate identity, without changing the earlier immutable USED or fabricating an extra declaration summary. This is existing approved per-admission authority, not a fifth no-decision variant or a wire change. Every other USAGE requires its actual scoped RELEASE.",

Rows are written in the same transaction as the dispatch state change on both paths: one RELEASE row per release including every retry (two rows, two `attempt_id`s on a forced retry); One immutable USAGE summary per declared secret under actual owner/attempt/declaration identity is required even for uncertain termination. Known USED may be committed early from verified PROGRESS; unknown and negative usage settle at terminal. Terminal reconciliation recognizes an already committed USED and never creates a second summary. Release/retry/live-recheck events do not create a second usage summary. Guided uses authentic ledger/admission evidence; replay uses authentic sparse `RunnerReport.secretUse`. Wire status remains exactly `USED|NOT_USED|REFUSED`: USED requires positive completed-use evidence, NOT_USED positive no-invocation/unreached evidence, REFUSED positive pre-effect refusal evidence. Missing child result, interrupted effect, mid-step kill or absent entry cannot synthesize NOT_USED or REFUSED. Resolved-but-proven-never-typed remains linked NOT_USED. Actual RELEASE and linked USAGE retain a nonnull resolution `outcome` from exactly `RESOLVED|NOT_AUTHORIZED|REVOKED|UNAVAILABLE|VAULT_UNAVAILABLE|REVOKED_MID_RUN`; RELEASE forbids usage_outcome and USAGE requires it. Audit-only uncertainty for released replay is one USAGE linked to its actual scoped RELEASE with `usage_outcome=UNKNOWN_OUTCOME`, or ACK_LOST only when acknowledgement loss is actually evidenced; neither is a wire status, a resolution outcome, a claimed usage fact or replay authority. Preserve positively committed usage facts. For observed replay, an authenticated PROGRESS report may carry only positively evidenced USED entries in the existing sparse secretUse map. Persist them only in the winning exact execution/accepted-history/attempt/admission/runnerInstance/sequence CAS transaction, after joining the frozen accepted artifact recipe and an actual completed secret-fill PASS receipt in the report. STARTED carries no usage facts; NOT_USED/REFUSED remain terminal-only. Arbitrary runner text, missing keys, failed/started steps, wrong recipes/attempts and payload reduction without supporting receipts cannot establish use. Later FINAL loss, cancel/reaper/unknown or sparse omission cannot overwrite already committed USED. No new wire field or status is introduced. Guided completion retains conservative OK→USED and every non-success→UNKNOWN_OUTCOME for each actual linked consumed secret admission; trusted backend no-send and authentic unreached facts retain their separately proven REFUSED/NOT_USED paths. A generic ledger ACK_LOST label alone never establishes actual acknowledgement loss. The present closed guided wire intentionally cannot transmit every private prewrite/post-fill fact; this does not authorize guessing. Prior committed positive facts remain immutable. No BridgeOutcome.secretUse field is added in this scope; any future completeness extension needs a separate explicit Aria proposal, fresh PO revalidation and root release. Three distinct no-decision variants are permitted: (1) true guided declared-but-unreached has one unlinked terminal USAGE/NOT_USED with null outcome/release_id/admission_id/vault_version/coordinate_ordinal and no fabricated release sequence. Its source_reference_id is the exact immutable configurationReferences.referenceId, coordinate_step_id is the declared source step, attempt is session:actual terminal owner fence, and full session/principal/CSI/environment/test/secret scope is authenticated against the immutable manifest and hash. A semantic obligation occurrence or selected-plan ordinal is never an actual action ordinal. Uniqueness is per actual declaration, independent of caller ordinal, sequence, timestamp or retention month. Distinct authentic source-reference declarations stay distinct. (2) guided committed consume with no committed resolution/release decision has one unlinked terminal uncertainty USAGE/UNKNOWN_OUTCOME (ACK_LOST only with separately authenticated actual acknowledgement-loss evidence), null outcome/release_id/vault_version and no fabricated release sequence, its actual nonnull admission_id/coordinate_step_id/coordinate_ordinal, dispatchCount1 and exact proposal→sourceInput→immutable reference/owner-fence binding. This variant may have had an ephemeral Vault read before crash: null means no committed decision, never zero reads or NOT_USED. (3) accepted OBSERVED_REPLAY declared-but-unattempted has one unlinked USAGE/NOT_USED only for an exact accepted execution/binding/revision/attempt/declared secret whose actual resolver path positively proves zero value-read entry for that ID and whose backend-owned atomic pre-send close or outage requeue proves transport was never entered. Outcome/release_id/vault_version/admission_id/guided coordinates are null; no release sequence is invented. The durable names-only no-send receipt and absence row commit with the owner transition. Missing decisionFacts, missing FINAL, post-send/no-admission ambiguity or a crash after possible read is insufficient. Other pre-send decisions, including genuine resolved-but-refused values, retain actual linked RELEASE/REFUSED facts. Retry authority stays separate: only existing genuine Vault-outage or definite transport refusal can authorize fresh attempt/grant/CAS; an absence receipt never grants retry. No admission/version/decision/release is fabricated and no extra Vault read or send is made for bookkeeping. Every other USAGE requires its actual scoped RELEASE. Preserve all actual release locator/timestamp/scope/owner/attempt/sequence/admission/coordinate/secret/version checks, unique write-once LIVE_RECHECK revocation events, duplicate/concurrent summary refusal and cross-month timestamp-evasion defenses. Unlinked timestamps are retention locators only, never fictional release times. Null actual RELEASE/linked-USAGE outcomes, malformed or wrong-scope links and spurious absence/admissions are refused. Append-only UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE, existing partition/bootstrap/pruner and Q3 retention constraints stand. Actual C-11 controller crashes before resolve and after read/pre-decision, replay child kills mid-fill/missing result, final-callback/reaper/cancel/revocation races and positive USED/NOT_USED/REFUSED cases use real resolver/send counters, fixture keystrokes and PostgreSQL facts; retain all audit value-canary scans. Retention: the existing retention pruner window (design §8 Q3 default). DDL authored by @data-engineer as `V34__studio_guided_secret_login.sql` on the **current** baseline; OBS-012A re-homes it into `V17__secret_use_audit` (ADR-SC-005 D-B). [design §4.1, §4.6 I-C10, §6 \"Migration\"; security review F-8]",

Rows are written in the same transaction as the dispatch state change on both paths: one RELEASE row per release including every retry (two rows, two `attempt_id`s on a forced retry); One immutable USAGE summary per declared secret under actual owner/attempt/declaration identity is required even for uncertain termination. Known USED may be committed early from verified PROGRESS; unknown and negative usage settle at terminal. Terminal reconciliation recognizes an already committed USED and never creates a second summary. Release/retry/live-recheck events do not create a second usage summary. Guided uses authentic ledger/admission evidence; replay uses authentic sparse `RunnerReport.secretUse`. Wire status remains exactly `USED|NOT_USED|REFUSED`: USED requires positive completed-use evidence, NOT_USED positive no-invocation/unreached evidence, REFUSED positive pre-effect refusal evidence. Missing child result, interrupted effect, mid-step kill or absent entry cannot synthesize NOT_USED or REFUSED. Resolved-but-proven-never-typed remains linked NOT_USED. Actual RELEASE and linked USAGE retain a nonnull resolution `outcome` from exactly `RESOLVED|NOT_AUTHORIZED|REVOKED|UNAVAILABLE|VAULT_UNAVAILABLE|REVOKED_MID_RUN`; RELEASE forbids usage_outcome and USAGE requires it. Audit-only uncertainty for released replay is one USAGE linked to its actual scoped RELEASE with `usage_outcome=UNKNOWN_OUTCOME`, or ACK_LOST only when acknowledgement loss is actually evidenced; neither is a wire status, a resolution outcome, a claimed usage fact or replay authority. Preserve positively committed usage facts. For observed replay, an authenticated PROGRESS report may carry only positively evidenced USED entries in the existing sparse secretUse map. Persist them only in the winning exact execution/accepted-history/attempt/admission/runnerInstance/sequence CAS transaction, after joining the frozen accepted artifact recipe and an actual completed secret-fill PASS receipt in the report. STARTED carries no usage facts; NOT_USED/REFUSED remain terminal-only. Arbitrary runner text, missing keys, failed/started steps, wrong recipes/attempts and payload reduction without supporting receipts cannot establish use. Later FINAL loss, cancel/reaper/unknown or sparse omission cannot overwrite already committed USED. No new wire field or status is introduced. Guided completion retains conservative OK→USED and every non-success→UNKNOWN_OUTCOME for each actual linked consumed secret admission; trusted backend no-send and authentic unreached facts retain their separately proven REFUSED/NOT_USED paths. A generic ledger ACK_LOST label alone never establishes actual acknowledgement loss. The present closed guided wire intentionally cannot transmit every private prewrite/post-fill fact; this does not authorize guessing. Prior committed positive facts remain immutable. No BridgeOutcome.secretUse field is added in this scope; any future completeness extension needs a separate explicit Aria proposal, fresh PO revalidation and root release. Three distinct no-decision variants are permitted: (1) true guided declared-but-unreached has one unlinked terminal USAGE/NOT_USED with null outcome/release_id/admission_id/vault_version/coordinate_ordinal and no fabricated release sequence. Its source_reference_id is the exact immutable configurationReferences.referenceId, coordinate_step_id is the declared source step, attempt is session:actual terminal owner fence, and full session/principal/CSI/environment/test/secret scope is authenticated against the immutable manifest and hash. A semantic obligation occurrence or selected-plan ordinal is never an actual action ordinal. Uniqueness is per actual declaration, independent of caller ordinal, sequence, timestamp or retention month. Distinct authentic source-reference declarations stay distinct. (2) guided committed consume with no committed resolution/release decision has one unlinked terminal uncertainty USAGE/UNKNOWN_OUTCOME (ACK_LOST only with separately authenticated actual acknowledgement-loss evidence), null outcome/release_id/vault_version and no fabricated release sequence, its actual nonnull admission_id/coordinate_step_id/coordinate_ordinal, dispatchCount1 and exact proposal→sourceInput→immutable reference/owner-fence binding. This variant may have had an ephemeral Vault read before crash: null means no committed decision, never zero reads or NOT_USED. (3) accepted OBSERVED_REPLAY declared-but-unattempted has one unlinked USAGE/NOT_USED only for an exact accepted execution/binding/revision/attempt/declared secret whose actual resolver path positively proves zero value-read entry for that ID and whose backend-owned atomic pre-send close or outage requeue proves transport was never entered. Outcome/release_id/vault_version/admission_id/guided coordinates are null; no release sequence is invented. The durable names-only no-send receipt and absence row commit with the owner transition. Missing decisionFacts, missing FINAL, post-send/no-admission ambiguity or a crash after possible read is insufficient. Other pre-send decisions, including genuine resolved-but-refused values, retain actual linked RELEASE/REFUSED facts. Retry authority stays separate: only existing genuine Vault-outage or definite transport refusal can authorize fresh attempt/grant/CAS; an absence receipt never grants retry. No admission/version/decision/release is fabricated and no extra Vault read or send is made for bookkeeping. Every other USAGE requires its actual scoped RELEASE. Preserve all actual release locator/timestamp/scope/owner/attempt/sequence/admission/coordinate/secret/version checks, unique write-once LIVE_RECHECK revocation events, duplicate/concurrent summary refusal and cross-month timestamp-evasion defenses. Unlinked timestamps are retention locators only, never fictional release times. Null actual RELEASE/linked-USAGE outcomes, malformed or wrong-scope links and spurious absence/admissions are refused. Append-only UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE, existing partition/bootstrap/pruner and Q3 retention constraints stand. Actual C-11 controller crashes before resolve and after read/pre-decision, replay child kills mid-fill/missing result, final-callback/reaper/cancel/revocation races and positive USED/NOT_USED/REFUSED cases use real resolver/send counters, fixture keystrokes and PostgreSQL facts; retain all audit value-canary scans. Retention: the existing retention pruner window (design §8 Q3 default). DDL authored by @data-engineer as `V34__studio_guided_secret_login.sql` on the **current** baseline; OBS-012A re-homes it into `V17__secret_use_audit` (ADR-SC-005 D-B). [design §4.1, §4.6 I-C10, §6 \"Migration\"; security review F-8]",

Terminal reconciliation recognizes an already committed USED and never creates a second summary. Release/retry/live-recheck events do not create a second usage summary. Guided uses authentic ledger/admission evidence; replay uses authentic sparse `RunnerReport.secretUse`. Wire status remains exactly `USED|NOT_USED|REFUSED`: USED requires positive completed-use evidence, NOT_USED positive no-invocation/unreached evidence, REFUSED positive pre-effect refusal evidence. docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/translation-design.md:93:**Late accounting without revival:** existing `settleModel` is active/owner guarded and cannot settle after cancellation/expiry. Do not weaken those guards. Retain the already charged reservation ceiling, mark the attempt abandoned/superseded, and append an immutable, attempt-scoped late-usage receipt through the translation store under its own accounting-only authorization. That operation can record numeric usage and whether known input/output exceeds the original reservation; it cannot change session state, plan head, owner, source, ledger or admission. Billing/evaluation reporting joins each reservation with its one accepted usage receipt and reports `max(reserved, known actual)` once per token category, so known overage is visible rather than described as capped or zero. Unknown actual usage remains explicitly unknown. If the session is still active but authority changed, continuation stays blocked until the current authorized coordinator reconciles accounting through the existing service; if that cannot safely occur, stop the run. A terminal session stays terminal. This is audit/reconciliation, not a second session budget counter or fresh send permit.

docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/translation-design.md:124:Replanning may refine unresolved interpretation and add a genuinely missing required private producer read before leaving its source state. It cannot append a duplicate obligation to justify replay of exercised work. Validate refinements against immutable accepted occurrence/source associations, operation/target/reference meaning and the complete exercised obligation set, not just model names. Legitimate distinct repeated operations require distinct source-supported occurrence identities admitted before their effects; they are not deduplicated merely because both use the same button. Unsupported or ambiguous repeat intent causes clarification/refusal rather than authorizing a speculative second effect. These structural associations and tests constrain interpretation without proving arbitrary-English equivalence.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/translation-design.md:134:`GuidedStepVerifier` is a real OBS-005 implementation installed through `GuidedProductionSessionAccess implements GuidedSessionService.StepVerifier`. It compares immutable source-associated obligations with all admitted/exercised action ordinals, exact input/binding associations, actual target/operation/assertion results and outstanding dependencies. Fail on missing submit/action obligation, changed assertion polarity, wrong span/input association, failed/unknown outcome, omitted producer or exercised operation absent from the accepted step plan. A typed VERIFY_STEP provider request may flag interpretation mismatch/ambiguity; it shares the model budget and cannot override a deterministic rejection, grant authority or convert failure into success. A provider's complete=true is never sufficient for `completeStep`.

Exact Unicode spans, two uses of same variable, mismatched step/slot/revision, forged safe flag, wrong destination, duplicate reference, immutable IDs/hash and no after-effect allocation. Source ambiguity uses real production v2 source question and public answer. |
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/translation-design.md:169:| Accounting | Actual PostgreSQL reservations/attempts/settlements; simultaneous requests, translator-lease/worker-fence races, crash before/after send, missing usage, overage, exhaustion before repair, cancellation/expiry and late provider reply. Prove one live attempt, immutable late-usage reporting with retained reservation and no revival, and no uncharged retry or application after budget failure. |
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/translation-design.md:170:| Database integrity | Real independent PostgreSQL connections and direct-SQL probes: missing required JSON keys/NULL, changed immutable manifest/question/plan, cross-session FKs, duplicate reservation/live attempt, rollback between reserve/attempt or question/mapping/answer writes, mixed source/configuration snapshot attempts, and two-session/source-edit lock-order/deadlock cases. |
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/translation-design.md:184:Independent Dara advice has been incorporated: immutable current-source manifests and plan revisions, one-live-attempt constraint, session-first lock order, atomic accounting/acceptance, immutable late-usage audit without session revival, atomic question/answer mapping and direct-SQL/race evidence. Concrete review items before a new PO verdict are the coordinated shared-file reservation, verification of the V32/session-lock amendments against that advice, and independent architecture/QA review of the new pre-materialization question phase and transport extraction. No new user decision is pending. Verify V32 availability before coding. Production account handoff and exact publication are known later dependencies, not unresolved OBS-005 design placeholders. If review finds a concrete inconsistency, record it and retain Draft until remediated; never silently weaken a privacy, source/slot or real-bridge requirement to obtain readiness.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/translation-design.md:242:// immutable association result keys: obligationId,admissionKey,proposal,admissionId (nullable)
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/translation-design.md:249:Attempt identity binds session scope/source/configuration, worker ID/fence, observation document/generation/evidence, plan revision and translator lease. Same request/attempt returns existing metadata with send=false; a live different attempt refuses. `claimSend` CAS consumes the one send right; old CALLING after crash is never resendable. `finishAttempt` closes live status with APPLIED/REJECTED/SUPERSEDED/UNKNOWN_CALL; rejected/unknown attempts retain accounting. `acceptPlan` receives server IDs in `plan.obligations` and validates immutable existing obligations against replacements; no deletion of admitted/exercised obligations. `reserveObligation` may only select a known admitted obligation and same meaning; its actual admission link commits with the existing ledger insert. The lead validates remaining semantics before calling it. Session terminal authority is never modified by usage auditing.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/translation-design.md:269:Provider schemas are selected per request kind, self-contained with compact local `$defs` references, and projected to the pinned SDK's supported subset. Strict local validation remains authoritative. Reservations include escaped content, the actual supplied schema and bounded SDK framing; settlement retains ceilings and charges known overage. An active session reconciles immutable late usage deltas once into its existing counters before another send, using private receipt identities; a terminal session is never revived and has only immutable usage reporting. Expired unresolved attempts remain charged and cannot reuse old send authority.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/translation-design.md:271:Observed clarification choices bind one current remaining obligation. Public answer acceptance and semantic mapping are atomic. Fresh requests receive the accepted safe locator/label, while the runner must re-establish correspondence against new observation; old node IDs grant no authority. The chosen locator can refine the target description while operation, source/value and scope remain bound to the same immutable obligation. Source questions remain pre-materialization and cannot fabricate a browser document. Dependency refinement keeps the frozen input references and admitted obligations; only a needed current-source private read can be appended, never a repeated effect or a late read from a departed page.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/translation-design.md:277:The guided adapter accounts reported input as `promptTokenCount + toolUsePromptTokenCount` and output as `candidatesTokenCount + thoughtsTokenCount`. Cached prompt tokens are already included in the prompt count and are never added again. Absent primary prompt/candidate counts remain unknown; optional tool/thought counts contribute when reported. Negative counts, integer overflow and inconsistent reported totals fail the call with unknown usage, retaining its conservative reservation. No thought content is accessed or logged. Actual HTTP metadata fixtures and joined PostgreSQL/Chromium cases exercise combined-output overage and immutable late usage after source drift. This follows the provider's [UsageMetadata definition](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/reference/rest/v1/GenerateContentResponse#UsageMetadata); legacy FULL/PATCH accounting is unchanged.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/translation-design.md:279:The OBS-003 foundation migration fixture explicitly targets V31 and retains its 30-migration assertion. OBS-005 separately tests an unrestricted fresh installation including V32, as well as V31-to-V32 preservation. The earlier broad run's stale foundation expectation remains recorded as a failure, followed by successful named correction reruns; it is not relabelled as a passing final-source broad run.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/translation-design.md:283:Inventory before implementation: SEC-001 (selected source is merely an unused-list member), REL-001 (scanner skips durable materialization/bootstrap), REL-002 (late usage can commit between entry reconciliation and send), TEST-001 (missing hostile current-page/NEXT_ACTION semantic corpus). The independent FAIL gate/probes and original development artifacts remain immutable historical evidence. This remediation is within OBS-005; account/publication ports remain later stories.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/translation-design.md:287:Replace a source-question choice's bare reference meaning with a closed `{need, reference}` meaning. `need` is the disputed `{stepId, occurrence, operationKind, argumentSlot}`; `occurrence` is the bounded semantic operation ordinal already used by SOURCE_PLAN obligations, and `argumentSlot` must equal the server's operation-to-slot mapping. All alternatives must have the same need and each reference must name that step/slot. No English parser or confidence threshold establishes this identity. The server validates source membership, operation capability and ordinal limits, then atomically persists the need with all alternatives in existing immutable clarification contexts. The public answer DTO remains unchanged; the public question coordinate displays the actual disputed step/occurrence rather than always the first step/zero. A second question cannot redefine an already accepted use.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/translation-design.md:289:At plan admission, require exactly one obligation at the selected need's step/occurrence with the same operation and slot, no runtime need substitution, and `sourceReferences[referenceIndex]` exactly equal to the chosen reference. Including the selected reference unused is rejected. The admitted server obligation UUID subsequently identifies this use; action validation independently rechecks the persisted selection against the current plan/use before its existing exact input-ID/operation checks. Replan preservation retains the chosen use. A choice for one occurrence cannot authorize any other occurrence. Strict model/context schemas and output contract change together; source manifests pin the new schemas/provider projection/output contract and old-pin continuation refuses. Existing immutable JSON storage accommodates the richer meaning without changing V32 or the public answer wire.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/translation-design.md:295:Use existing translation continuation plus private session progress `translationBootstrap` for explicit stages: `PLAN_ACCEPTED`, `MATERIALIZED`, `ALLOCATED`, `CONTEXT_PENDING`, `READY`. Each stage records the accepted source/scope/fence and plan/context identity when available; updates occur under the existing session lock. No new SQL enum/table/migration or runner contract is needed. Accept plan and `PLAN_ACCEPTED`/`MATERIALIZE` atomically. Resume exact idempotent materialization under its existing key; commit `MATERIALIZED` after successful materialization, allowing a crash between the actual commit and stage marker to re-read the existing immutable result. Replay dependency allocation only under its existing stable need keys; atomically save trusted binding IDs/plan revision and `ALLOCATED`. Persist `CONTEXT_PENDING` before network context delivery.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/translation-design.md:299:Actual `continueRuns()` fault tests interrupt after accepted plan, after materialization, and after a persisted NEXT with still-pending first context. They must retain one provider SOURCE_PLAN send, one immutable materialization, stable allocations and acknowledged initial evidence before any NEXT_ACTION request; real owning worker authentication remains in use. Post-effect missing context/outcome is terminal, not a browser recreation or dispatch replay.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/translation-design.md:303:Extract accounting-only reconciliation that accepts the already locked session, applies each immutable usage-audit delta once and persists counters/terminal stop. Every attempt reservation transaction and every send-claim transaction invokes it while holding that same session lock, including repair and expired-attempt recovery iterations. Late-receipt writers already acquire the session lock; retain that ordering. A stopped decision is returned from the transaction and refused only after commit, never thrown inside the accounting transaction. Terminal sessions may acquire additional immutable numeric accounting but cannot become active or authorize a send. Route-entry reconciliation remains an optimization, not authority. Preserve thought/tool/cache numeric handling, conservative unknown reservations, original attempt fences and one-send claim.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/translation-design.md:321:READY will require both the existing authenticated initial-blank evidence and a successful existing same-context metadata RPC acknowledgement. Before each delivery, commit a private bounded delivery attempt and the exact pending identity/context/materialization/input-hash/allocation snapshot under the session lock. Check current source, pins, owner/fence, no actions and pending/current equality before network I/O. After the RPC returns successfully, recheck those identities and require the acknowledgement's existing bridge identity to match; persist a private `metadataAcknowledgement` containing the delivery attempt ID and canonical pending-context hash in the same transaction as READY. No callback, regardless of arrival time, can populate that marker. No new callback field, runner API, schema or migration is needed.

docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/bridge-design.md:3:Date: 2026-10-08. Status: coordinated architecture remediation for Draft STUDIO-OBS-004/005; not a readiness or QA verdict. This document specifies future implementation. No endpoint, schema, migration or runtime behavior described here is claimed implemented.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/bridge-design.md:19:Reserved/unreleased v1 files and completed-story evidence remain historical; this does not impose production-v1 backward compatibility or claim a deployed-v1 migration. Preserve the functioning legacy one-shot/replay lane and its version constants. Artifact v2/reference-policy 3 remain separate OBS-006 deliverables: observed-2 transport support alone never marks an artifact ready. Later stories must consume the selected tuple. Do not edit historical OBS-001/002/003 stories or gates to imply their tests covered this bridge.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/bridge-design.md:30:For initial blank, the backend resolves a destination input from immutable authored/configuration provenance, verifies source-step association and destination policy, then admits the typed navigate operation through the same ledger and action budget. The worker rechecks original page identity and blankness during prepare and immediately before dispatch. Success leads to OBSERVING, where the existing approved-origin collector produces the first actual page observation. Redirects remain subject to destination/network policy. Failure or uncertainty never repeats the navigation.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/bridge-design.md:37:2. `operationHash = SHA256(canonical-v1({coordinate, origin, locator, operation}))`. Here `origin` is the actual pre-action document origin: JSON null for initialBlank and canonical HTTP(S) otherwise. Initial navigation has `locator: null`; its destination remains an immutable destination input ID in `operation`. Never substitute destination origin for the nonexistent source origin.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/bridge-design.md:45:The backend is the sole orchestrator. It holds gateway credentials and obtains executable proposals from its immutable admission store. The worker has no gateway capability.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/bridge-design.md:61:4. Admission stores the exact proposal and immutable ledger. The backend dispatch service invokes a v2 consume operation whose in-process result is a discriminated union: `WonConsumption(storedProposal, storedLedger, preparationId)` or `AlreadyConsumed(storedLedger)`/refusal. Only the transaction that changes ADMITTED/count=0 to DISPATCHING/count=1 returns WonConsumption after successful commit.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/bridge-design.md:65:8. `/outcomes` is owner-authenticated and compared to immutable stored admission. Duplicate dispatch messages return journal status and never call the browser twice. Duplicate outcomes are identical-only. Lost winning response, dispatch acknowledgement or callback does not cause automatic navigation/click/read repetition. Conservatively stop UNKNOWN_OUTCOME when consumption happened but completion is not known.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/bridge-design.md:71:Worker `/lifecycle` carries bounded reason and identity metadata for lost acknowledgement, lost context and teardown; the backend validates current owner/fence and invokes existing trusted lostAcknowledgment handling. Backend cancellation/expiry commits revocation of future unconsumed work, then sends idempotent `/stop`. Worker serializes stop with its local dispatch gate, rejects new work, closes the browser and destroys the value map. Independently enforced local lease and immutable session deadline stop the worker if notifications cannot arrive. Lease renewal never extends expiresAt; renewal carries current control state and cannot revive terminal work.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/bridge-design.md:77:OBS-004 owns trusted source-reference validation, allocation, storage/materialization primitives and protocol validation. OBS-005 owns semantic source interpretation and dependency planning. Their common input is a candidate reference union: an exact immutable source span (`stepId`, exclusive-end UTF-16 offsets, kind and intended slot), or an authorized immutable configuration reference. Neither variant carries proposed literal bytes or model-issued input IDs. OBS-004 validates revision/bounds/Unicode boundaries, approved nonsecret source classification, type/slot/scope and destination policy, then slices or resolves the authoritative source, allocates server IDs and freezes the table/hash. Classification comes from the approved source/configuration boundary; no new automatic classifier is assumed. Invalid or unclassified references fail closed. Extend Snapshot/source handling to retain these immutable identities. Never infer the table from arbitrary action text or copy a model-generated literal.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/bridge-design.md:79:This common contract is independent of whether a model may see the author's literal text: both privacy branches ultimately supply the same candidate provenance references. OBS-004 tests must supply controlled immutable source/configuration and classified span/reference proposals, then exercise actual validation, allocation, hashing, persistence and authenticated materialization, rather than injecting a finished fabricated table. They do not claim production arbitrary-English extraction. OBS-005 alone supplies the semantic candidate-selection mechanism and chosen outbound source projection. Its unresolved mechanism is an explicit later dependency of the complete product, not a prerequisite for proving OBS-004 transport. No model-facing source projection or privacy policy is implemented by OBS-004; shared source-reference and runner transport fields have identical semantics in both branches.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/bridge-design.md:84:- Producer evidence: actual admitted read coordinate, recipe, origin and immutable producer admission, derived by the backend from its stored proposal and successful outcome. The outcome additionally carries only a local-availability receipt bound to live context/binding/admission. No value, sample, length or value digest crosses the worker boundary. Store this atomically with successful read completion; duplicate receipts cannot rewrite provenance.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/bridge-design.md:97:The gateway may receive immutable author-written nonsecret English, including literals the author intentionally typed, but never resolved saved-variable values, credentials or runtime/page captures. Preserve opaque existing configuration references without expansion in source/context/repair payloads. Classification still rejects secret-looking/declared-sensitive source; this is not permission to send arbitrary secrets typed into English.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/bridge-design.md:101:Resolve authorized nonsecret saved configuration references only inside trusted backend handling and runner materialization; credentials remain separate. Freeze the complete input table/hash before the first application action. Later proposals refer to IDs/type/source-step metadata. New literal allocation after effects is not a mutable-table escape: unresolved association must use already frozen valid provenance or stop and require a newly prepared immutable session.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/bridge-design.md:113:OBS-004 owns v2 bridge/source-reference contract/API/checker implementation, backend session/bridge persistence and transport, runtime compatibility, runner prepare/pinning/journal/lifecycle, and concrete materialization/producer/consumer metadata. OBS-005 owns the source-span semantic resolver, gateway/dependency orchestration, durable clarification semantic mapping, step verification and model evaluation. INPUT-POLICY-01 is resolved; OBS-005 owns the reserved model-facing schemas/examples and production question contract under the sequential ownership specified in its story and translation design. It must not change the completed common transport to relax confidentiality. Exact reserved file lists are recorded in the paired stories. Historical OBS-004 migration ownership was V31. V30/V31 are now frozen; OBS-005 reserves V32 for additive translation state after confirming availability. Other shared contract/service changes after OBS-004 require coordinated ownership amendment, not parallel edits.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/bridge-design.md:123:Dispatch entry must reject an ambient transaction. The dedicated consume transaction must finish its real commit before the ephemeral winner result can authorize a send; the current REQUIRED TransactionTemplate can otherwise return inside an uncommitted outer transaction. Commit/rollback failure sends nothing. Never persist a winner response in generic idempotency storage; same-key/new-key retries are historical AlreadyConsumed results. Obtain the executable proposal from immutable storage. Tests must cover actual independent database connections and synchronized races, rollback and cache/restart replay.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/bridge-design.md:125:Persist authenticated network preparation results in a short transaction, then admission atomically checks current source/account/policy, proof/input/context identities, budgets and binding prerequisites; attach the proof and consumer edges in that transaction. Fix one authoritative-source/configuration/session/bridge lock order. Read success atomically updates the immutable-ledger outcome fields, inserts a separate producer receipt, advances materialization revision and deduplicates. Changed duplicate receipts conflict even if the reported ledger is equal. V30 forbids later receipt additions to ledger JSON; preserve that protection. Use named action INSERT columns if schema columns change.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/bridge-design.md:127:Cancellation/expiry invalidates unused proofs and live context atomically; successful historical producer evidence is never current local availability after teardown. Prove no lost allocation/revision under concurrent replans, no edge before committed producer success, no resurrection in cancel/callback/takeover races, and actual source/configuration row locking. Include fresh-install and V30-to-V31 migration tests; OBS-004 owns corresponding migration-test updates. These implementation constraints refine the accepted bridge without choosing INPUT-POLICY-01 or widening product scope.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/bridge-design.md:151:Before ownership exists, backend persists one immutable assignment intent in private session progress under the current authorization/source/session lock, then sends authenticated runner `/assign` outside the transaction. The request binds assignment/session/worker IDs, scope/source/configuration identities, exact versions, expected fence and immutable expiry. Acquisition has no X-Owner-Fence header. Runner reserves capacity and fsyncs a separate assignment tombstone before calling existing backend `/claim` with its own mounted issuer-provided worker JWT and mTLS. The bounded typed202 response must validate the complete session, scope hash, source/configuration, run authorization, tuple, hard deadline and actual owner/fence; HTTP success alone is insufficient. A value-free200 OWNED receipt reports only validated assignment/owner/lease identity. Backend verifies it against storage, then materializes inputs and sends context. No browser launches before a live matching assignment and complete context. V2 claim must match the persisted assigned worker/intent; preserve historical v1 behavior.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/bridge-design.md:153:The worker renews about every10 seconds for the existing30-second lease, including before context and during actions/clarification. One request may be outstanding; every renewal uses a fresh idempotency key and current fence, a total timeout shorter than remaining acknowledged authority, and the mounted token reread for rotation. Only a validated same-owner/fence/scope claim acknowledgement may extend a still-live local lease within immutable expiry. Dedicated lease application does not wait on runtime.busy or reset workflow/materialization state. Delayed context metadata cannot decrease an acknowledged lease, and a later timestamp in context alone cannot extend it. Failure, lost response, expiry, terminal state or stop closes local authority; late replies never revive it.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/bridge-design.md:157:Exact additive schemas/unions and API examples are owned by the contract specialist; backend owns intent/client/claim guards/pre-context lifecycle and joined tests; runner owns registry, typed claim client, timers, local lease ordering and tombstones. Final real mTLS/PostgreSQL/Chromium evidence must show actual-worker initial acquisition, a run alive beyond one30-second lease, renewal during pauses/work, duplicate/capacity behavior, failed or stale renewal, hard expiry, stop before context and restart refusal. Use an immutable hashed runner-build snapshot for the final joined tests to avoid concurrent-build ambiguity.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/bridge-design.md:187:OBS-005 persistence refinement incorporates independent Dara advice in translation design §5: additive V32 source manifests/immutable plan revisions, fenced one-live-attempt accounting, atomic question/answer meaning and immutable late-usage audit. Existing V30/V31 and active-only settlement authority remain intact; expired or cancelled sessions never regain execution authority through a late provider response.

docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/secret-login-design.md:108:**4.1 Audit (SEC-9).** New append-only table `studio_secret_use_audit(id, occurred_at, path ∈ {GUIDED,OBSERVED_REPLAY}, execution_id?, session_id?, admission_id?, principal_id, csi_id, environment, test_id, secret_id, vault_version?, outcome ∈ {RESOLVED,NOT_AUTHORIZED,REVOKED,UNAVAILABLE,VAULT_UNAVAILABLE,REVOKED_MID_RUN})`, UPDATE/DELETE refused by trigger, written in the same transaction as the dispatch state change (replay: beside `recordDispatchPolicy`, `StudioDispatcher.java:322`). Never a value. Retention: existing retention pruner window unless Security asks otherwise (§8 Q3). T2 acceptance boundary: One immutable USAGE summary per declared secret under actual owner/attempt/declaration identity is required even for uncertain termination. Known USED may be committed early from verified PROGRESS; unknown and negative usage settle at terminal. Terminal reconciliation recognizes an already committed USED and never creates a second summary. Release/retry/live-recheck events do not create a second usage summary. Guided uses authentic ledger/admission evidence; replay uses authentic sparse `RunnerReport.secretUse`. Wire status remains exactly `USED|NOT_USED|REFUSED`: USED requires positive completed-use evidence, NOT_USED positive no-invocation/unreached evidence, REFUSED positive pre-effect refusal evidence. Missing child result, interrupted effect, mid-step kill or absent entry cannot synthesize NOT_USED or REFUSED. Resolved-but-proven-never-typed remains linked NOT_USED. Actual RELEASE and linked USAGE retain a nonnull resolution `outcome` from exactly `RESOLVED|NOT_AUTHORIZED|REVOKED|UNAVAILABLE|VAULT_UNAVAILABLE|REVOKED_MID_RUN`; RELEASE forbids usage_outcome and USAGE requires it. Audit-only uncertainty for released replay is one USAGE linked to its actual scoped RELEASE with `usage_outcome=UNKNOWN_OUTCOME`, or ACK_LOST only when acknowledgement loss is actually evidenced; neither is a wire status, a resolution outcome, a claimed usage fact or replay authority. Preserve positively committed usage facts. For observed replay, an authenticated PROGRESS report may carry only positively evidenced USED entries in the existing sparse secretUse map. Persist them only in the winning exact execution/accepted-history/attempt/admission/runnerInstance/sequence CAS transaction, after joining the frozen accepted artifact recipe and an actual completed secret-fill PASS receipt in the report. STARTED carries no usage facts; NOT_USED/REFUSED remain terminal-only. Arbitrary runner text, missing keys, failed/started steps, wrong recipes/attempts and payload reduction without supporting receipts cannot establish use. Later FINAL loss, cancel/reaper/unknown or sparse omission cannot overwrite already committed USED. No new wire field or status is introduced. Guided completion retains conservative OK→USED and every non-success→UNKNOWN_OUTCOME for each actual linked consumed secret admission; trusted backend no-send and authentic unreached facts retain their separately proven REFUSED/NOT_USED paths. A generic ledger ACK_LOST label alone never establishes actual acknowledgement loss. The present closed guided wire intentionally cannot transmit every private prewrite/post-fill fact; this does not authorize guessing. Prior committed positive facts remain immutable. No BridgeOutcome.secretUse field is added in this scope; any future completeness extension needs a separate explicit Aria proposal, fresh PO revalidation and root release. Four distinct guarded no-decision variants are permitted (all four use release_seq=NULL; actual linked release sequences remain unchanged): (1) true guided declared-but-unreached has one unlinked terminal USAGE/NOT_USED with null outcome/release_id/admission_id/vault_version/coordinate_ordinal and no fabricated release sequence. Its source_reference_id is the exact immutable configurationReferences.referenceId, coordinate_step_id is the declared source step, attempt is session:actual terminal owner fence, and full session/principal/CSI/environment/test/secret scope is authenticated against the immutable manifest and hash. A semantic obligation occurrence or selected-plan ordinal is never an actual action ordinal. Uniqueness is per actual declaration, independent of caller ordinal, sequence, timestamp or retention month. Distinct authentic source-reference declarations stay distinct. (2) guided committed consume with no committed resolution/release decision has one unlinked terminal uncertainty USAGE/UNKNOWN_OUTCOME (ACK_LOST only with separately authenticated actual acknowledgement-loss evidence), null outcome/release_id/vault_version and no fabricated release sequence, its actual nonnull admission_id/coordinate_step_id/coordinate_ordinal, dispatchCount1 and exact proposal→sourceInput→immutable reference/owner-fence binding. This variant may have had an ephemeral Vault read before crash: null means no committed decision, never zero reads or NOT_USED. (3) accepted OBSERVED_REPLAY declared-but-unattempted has one unlinked USAGE/NOT_USED only for an exact accepted execution/binding/revision/attempt/declared secret whose actual resolver path positively proves zero value-read entry for that ID and whose backend-owned atomic pre-send close or outage requeue proves transport was never entered. Outcome/release_id/vault_version/admission_id/guided coordinates are null; no release sequence is invented. The durable names-only no-send receipt and absence row commit with the owner transition. Missing decisionFacts, missing FINAL, post-send/no-admission ambiguity or a crash after possible read is insufficient. Other pre-send decisions, including genuine resolved-but-refused values, retain actual linked RELEASE/REFUSED facts. Retry authority stays separate: only existing genuine Vault-outage or definite transport refusal can authorize fresh attempt/grant/CAS; an absence receipt never grants retry. No admission/version/decision/release is fabricated and no extra Vault read or send is made for bookkeeping. For an accepted observed declaration with no actual committed DISPATCH resolution and no existing usage summary, variant (3) also permits a terminal-winner NOT_USED summary when an actual locked QUEUED/CLAIMED-to-DONE transition and a separate durable names-only terminal settlement receipt prove that no dispatch attempt/admission/observed admission receipt or transport entry existed, that every existing secret-value provider path was required to commit its exact scoped read-entry before entry, and that this ID had no such read-entry at the serialized terminal cut. A no-read classification is justified only by that universally enforced committed write-before-value-read protocol, the fresh serialized terminal view and the winning zero-send pre-send transition, never by missing FINAL/decision/marker rows alone; actual physical read counts remain independent executed test evidence. Read-entry acquisition and terminal closure serialize on the same owner row; no read may proceed if its required entry fails, and no new entry or RELEASE may be appended after settlement. An expired claimant is not impersonated as a live lease owner. The terminal winner authenticates the accepted history locator, immutable revision/declaration, exact binding digest/attempt and full scope. Its receipt, history/ledger transition and all new summaries commit or roll back in one physical transaction; deferred per-leaf guards verify the actual owner row version written by that transaction. This terminal-only proof grants no requeue, refreshRetry, deadline, grant, admission, dispatch or send authority. Existing live-owned completed-resolution CLOSED/REQUEUED receipts and their outage-only retry guards remain unchanged. (4) accepted OBSERVED_REPLAY declared secret with a durable exact-scoped read-entry but no committed DISPATCH resolution/release decision has one unlinked terminal USAGE/UNKNOWN_OUTCOME only with that same authenticated winning pre-send terminal transition and terminal settlement receipt. Null outcome/release_id/release_seq/vault_version/admission_id/source_reference_id/guided coordinates means no committed resolution, release or action identity, never zero physical reads or proven use/refusal. The accepted binding attempt_id is real and remains nonnull even when ledger dispatch attempt_id is absent. A read-entry proves possible provider entry only: it may precede a crash before the call or a real read whose decision was lost. Do not infer a Vault version or any of the six resolution outcomes, ACK_LOST, NOT_USED, REFUSED or USED from this marker or a terminal error label. Physically counted reads/sends and actual crash positions remain separate test evidence. Unlinked terminal identity is exact execution/accepted-history/attempt/declared secret, independent of timestamp, caller sequence, guessed ordinal or retention partition. Existing actual RELEASE links and immutable USED summaries always take precedence; never append an unlinked substitute or a second summary. Post-send/no-admission ambiguity stays on actual linked uncertainty and is excluded from the new pre-send proof. A dispatched declaration lacking its required actual RELEASE is a lineage defect requiring evidence/remediation, not permission to fabricate an unlinked row.  The separate append-only CLOSED-only studio_observed_terminal_secret_settlements receipt is distinct from studio_observed_no_send_decisions and never relaxes that live-owned completed-resolution guard. Before the state change, its database insertion guard captures and authenticates the actual locked pre-transition owner-row before-image and exact accepted binding/revision/declaration/scope. A caller-supplied preceding_state, terminal error label or insertion against an already-DONE row cannot establish this proof. After acquiring any waited-for owner lock, classify under a fresh authoritative post-lock read-entry view, not the stale statement snapshot. Terminal closure fences future read-entry, RELEASE and send; a provider call cannot proceed without its required committed exact-scope entry. Receipt, terminal history/ledger and all required summaries share the actual winning caller physical transaction. Deferred guards on each current/future leaf independently verify that transaction's actual terminal row version, exact locator/binding/attempt and complete declared-ID classification. Savepoint/subtransaction row-version behavior must be proven or prohibited; transaction labels or self-invoked proxy annotations are not proof. External caller rollback and injected receipt/audit failures roll back every write. All actual immediate-cancel, generic-close, pending-reaper and kill-switch terminal entrypoints must participate; admitted/running reconciliation settles authentic linked facts under its real terminal state matrix, never this pre-send unlinked shape. Request-only cancel, applied=0, stale or losing transitions append zero rows. Append-only UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE guards cover receipt parents and leaves, with no DEFAULT partition, aligned bounded existing 12-month Q3 retention, bootstrap/pruner coverage, stable cross-month deduplication and owner-row→owner-advisory→event lock order. No self-FK may prevent approved expiry; a same-transaction row version is not permanent identity. For these two unlinked replay cases outcome, release_id, release_seq, vault_version, admission_id, source_reference_id, coordinate_step_id and coordinate_ordinal are all NULL; the real accepted binding attempt_id is nonnull. The original three-variant null-release_seq rule remains and also applies to variant (4). Validate bounded unique disjoint no-read/possible-read ID sets against exactly the remaining authenticated accepted declarations, after excluding authentic existing decisions and summaries; no caller-chosen omission or invented ID is allowed. Durable entry is only possible-read evidence; the receipt/SQL does not measure a physical provider read. Without universal write-before-value-read enforcement, fresh-view classification or authenticated terminal/no-send proof, completeness remains unmet: emit no guessed negative. Known actual releases keep all scoped links/outcomes/version/sequence checks and honest linked settlement, including immutable early USED. A late loser cannot append its transient resolution facts after another terminal owner won. Existing GUIDED declaration absence checks continue to exclude any prior consumption/decision/summary across retained fences for that exact reference. A prior same-reference USED summary excludes a new unreached claim, but must not mask a later authentic consumed admission: settle that later admission under its existing actual linked or consumed-no-decision owner/admission/coordinate identity, without changing the earlier immutable USED or fabricating an extra declaration summary. This is existing approved per-admission authority, not a fifth no-decision variant or a wire change. Every other USAGE requires its actual scoped RELEASE. Preserve all actual release locator/timestamp/scope/owner/attempt/sequence/admission/coordinate/secret/version checks, unique write-once LIVE_RECHECK revocation events, duplicate/concurrent summary refusal and cross-month timestamp-evasion defenses. Unlinked timestamps are retention locators only, never fictional release times. Null actual RELEASE/linked-USAGE outcomes, malformed or wrong-scope links and spurious absence/admissions are refused. Append-only UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE, existing partition/bootstrap/pruner and Q3 retention constraints stand. Actual C-11 controller crashes before resolve and after read/pre-decision, replay child kills mid-fill/missing result, final-callback/reaper/cancel/revocation races and positive USED/NOT_USED/REFUSED cases use real resolver/send counters, fixture keystrokes and PostgreSQL facts; retain all audit value-canary scans. Linked actual RELEASE/USAGE keep their authentic positive release sequence; LIVE_RECHECK retains its approved affected-release lineage without inventing another sequence. The append-only backend-owned studio_observed_no_send_decisions receipt is keyed by (execution_id, execution_accepted_at, accepted_binding_attempt_id), bound to the accepted binding digest/revision/full scope and actual winning owner, and carries only bounded positively not-entered-for-value-read declared IDs, CLOSED or REQUEUED disposition and its own timestamp. Mark read entry before each existing value-read call; build the negative set only from the authenticated accepted declaration iterator and actual completed synchronous resolver/literal-verification control flow. Guard from locked authentic CLAIMED/current lease with no dispatch attempt/admission/observed receipt/sendCommitted; receipt, audit and winning close/outage-requeue commit together or all roll back. A guarded database transition constraint or equivalent database-verified owner interface prevents receipt-only commit; caller flags are insufficient. Keep owner row→owner advisory→event lock order, cross-month deduplication and Q3 receipt/audit retention alignment. The receipt provides no refreshRetry, deadline, grant or CAS authority: zero_send_decision_attempt_id remains limited to real VAULT_UNAVAILABLE outage CLAIMED→QUEUED provenance, definite_refusal_attempt_id to authentic transport refusal. Post-send/no-admission ambiguity is excluded. Supporting receipts are the existing RunnerReport.steps[] objects, exactly {stepIndex,status,startedAtMs,finishedAtMs,durationMs,failure}; they gain no stepId, sourceInputId, secretId, admission or other wire field. Applied=0, stale/late/losing reports append nothing; audit/report failure rolls back both. STARTED/PROGRESS keep outcome and evidence null. Payload reduction omits every newly unsupported positive when its PASS support is shed. Terminal negative/unknown settlement cannot overwrite a committed USED or append a second summary; a complete later cumulative report may recover omitted supported positives without another action/read. This exact §4.1 amendment governs I-C10 and C-11 references to §4.1: their historical two-variant and terminal-only summary prose is expanded only by the four guarded no-decision variants, the narrowly authenticated terminal-winner variant (3) proof and early verified replay USED above. docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/delayed-state-design.md:7:Wait only **before selecting/invoking the next already-admitted semantic operation**. A passive observation is not another action admission, assertion attempt, read capture, model proposal or dispatch. Once the retained target is selected, failed revalidation is terminal. Once invocation begins, it can never return to acquisition. No hidden replay, locator fallback, binding resampling, assertion retry, model WAIT variant, public DTO, migration or new account port.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/delayed-state-design.md:9:Actual collector ceilings remain 500 exported nodes, depth8, 32768 UTF-8 bytes, 50ms collection work, 4096 traversed elements and work depth64 (`observationSanitizer.ts`). Actual guided session defaults are 400 observations, 1,048,576 cumulative sanitized evidence bytes, 600 seconds, 200 actions, 100 model proposals, 128000/32000 reserved model input/output tokens (`GuidedSessionProperties`). Persisted per-session limits may be tighter and always win. `TestConfiguration.timeoutSeconds` is 1..120, default30; it is not currently in the immutable translation manifest. Do not invent a manifest timeout or change its historical hash.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/delayed-state-design.md:80:Guided passive-readiness allowance is cumulative **per source step**, equal to locked `ui_tests.timeout_seconds*1000` (1..120 seconds). At new translation initialization `GuidedTranslationStore.initialize` records that positive bounded value and actual source/configuration identities in private progress. Concrete `long stepTimeoutMillis(JsonNode session)` requires the existing session→ui_tests transaction/lock and exact test/source/config identities. No invented timeout manifest field, old hash rewrite, constructor/account dependency or migration. The allowance limits passive wait/collection windows only; it is not a new end-to-end learning SLA.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/delayed-state-design.md:114:Order in `next`: reconcile immutable late usage; validate source/pins/bootstrap; recover original in-flight obligation; reconcile deterministic completion; select current earliest unfulfilled server obligation; recover any exact pending acquisition; perform readiness; only then reserve/send NEXT_ACTION. There is no extra acquisition timeout imposed on a model call or human answer. Existing model send-claim checks source/plan/worker/lease/observation and also requires `window=null,pending=null`; it does not compare an old readiness-window deadline after that window was settled.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/delayed-state-design.md:155:No new schema/protocol/migration paths. Public observation, model request/response, source manifest and original action/admission payloads stay unchanged. Existing artifact2/plan/binding hashes remain immutable. This is a compatible observed execution bug fix, not a new executable operation; packaged reference/source/build/catalog identities must be regenerated and explicitly associated with the supported profile. Old local/production image attestation is not borrowed. New implementation must pass independent review of private classification and durable timing before production work; no live-provider accuracy claim or009 benchmark is included.

docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/publication-design.md:55:Current OBS-004/005 does **not** retain every original observation: progress overwrites it and preparation rows keep proofs without target facts. docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/publication-design.md:92:Session-wide three-attempt budget applies across keys and restarts.
